text:
alex: Running a concurrency sweep on redwood-v0-compact-int8 with kv-prefetch=true + int8 quant. At 48 concurrent workers p95 is fine (~320ms) but p99 jumped to ~680ms and cost/token spiked. Anyone seen this pattern?
mira: Which runner + harness commit? Also paste load shape and batching settings so we can repro.
alex: Runner v2.14.5, harness main@cb9a1e. Load: steady ramp to 48 workers, target qps ~120, tokens/window 512, batch_size=8. Config snippet below:
```
model: redwood-v0-compact-int8
runner: v2.14.5
kv_prefetch: true
batch_size: 8
window_tokens: 512
concurrency: 48
quant: int8
```
alex: Adding the small log excerpt where we see the p99 spike — lots of short stalls around token emission: "emit_delay_ms: [12, 9, 15, 102, 7, 680, 10]"
tj: Hmm that looks like an occasional huge emit delay. Could be lock contention or a retry/backoff from a secondary path. Any differences vs v2.14.4?
eva: We shipped a KV-cache prefetch refactor in v2.14.5 that changes the token accounting path slightly. I raised an eyebrow about double accounting in the perf review but couldn't repro locally.
mira: Can you run a diff of runner telemetry? Specifically: kvcache_hits, kvcache_misses, token_emit_delays histogram, and batch_fill_time. Small script: 
```
curl -s http://harness/metrics?snapshot=1 | jq '.metrics | {kvcache_hits, kvcache_misses, token_emit_delays, batch_fill_time}'
```
alex: Pasted snapshot — kvcache_misses up 3x on v2.14.5, token_emit_delays p99 large. Also noticed the harness reported "tokens_counted: 1.02x_expected" in the test-summary.
tj: "tokens_counted" > expected is interesting. If token accounting is off, cost per token calc and batching triggers could misbehave. Could prefetch path be incrementing the counter twice on some paths?
ci-bot: eval-sweep #482 finished: 1 failed (token-accounting.test), 24 passed. Logs: https://ci.internal/482
eva: Opening issue: https://go/repo/issues/432 "runner: double-count tokens when kv-prefetch triggers remote-fetch fallback". Assigning to infra/runner. Priority P0 for rollout revert decision.
mira: Short mitigation: revert runner to v2.14.4 in the staging eval fleet while infra investigates. Add a CI guard that fails on token-accounting.test to prevent merges.
alex: Spawning a quick smoke using v2.14.4 on the same load pattern now, will report in ~6m :hourglass_flowing_sand:.
tj: Also add a small unit test that simulates prefetch hit->fallback path and asserts tokens increment by exactly the number of produced tokens. That'll catch regressions earlier.
eva: Agreed. I'm adding the test to runner/test/token_accounting_test.go and gating it in CI.
alex: Quick update: with v2.14.4 p99 back to ~260ms, no cost spike. Reverting staging fleet now and scheduling a postmortem with infra + eng-ml for 30m from now.
mira: Good catch. Follow-ups: (1) revert in prod if we see this on prod sweeps, (2) patch v2.14.5 with token accounting fix, (3) add CI guard + unit test, (4) add a short telemetry check that alerts if tokens_counted > 1.01 * tokens_emitted for a sweep.
eva: I'll own the patch + issue. Adding label "root-cause: kvcache-prefetch-token-double-count".
alex: Thanks all — will paste final smoke logs in the issue. :thumbsup:
